unnumbered.review: Inspected main normative body (official windows-1252 HTML, decoded with mqtt5_normative_inventory), not Appendix B summaries. Broker FrameReader validates fixed flags, bounded Remaining Length, CONNECT deadline, ordered fields and end-of-frame; CONNECT reserved/Will flags are checked before registration. Client Connect::write composes defined flags, protocol name/version and length-prefixed fields. Server CONNECT Keep Alive zero disables protocol ping enforcement while a distinct 300s idle policy remains. A PINGRESP timeout recommendation is implemented by rumqttc state ping tracking, but timing under scheduler starvation was not dynamically evaluated.
unnumbered.limitations: Static source review only by this agent. No builds, tests, services, dependencies or Git commands. Timing/load/fragmentation exhaustiveness is not claimed. Historical CI 39164217059 belongs to broker db472bc/client 501cde2/admin 4483, not these baseline commits; no historical PASS was assigned to a row.

unnumbered.review: Broker mqtt5_connect_properties_supported checks property context, bounded VBI block and singleton uniqueness. Session Expiry defaults 0, Receive Maximum 65535 and Topic Alias Maximum 0; receive/packet size zero are rejected. Request Response/Problem flags are unique booleans; User Properties are repeatable UTF-8 pairs. Authentication Data without Method is a protocol error; duplicate method/data are rejected; unsupported methods get 0x8C after property checks. Informational CONNECT properties are intentionally consumed rather than forwarded. CLI validates ranges before configuring patched rumqttc. Response Information is never emitted; diagnostic strings/user properties are absent from broker control responses, so the server's Request Problem Information restriction is satisfied by omission.
unnumbered.limitations: The client can request Problem Information=0, but uniform handling of forbidden server diagnostics was not established (row 3.1.2-29 EVIDENCE_GAP). This does not assert that a single ignored informational property is a security issue. Property context/error handling is inspected, not a dynamic full matrix.

unnumbered.section: 3.1.3 (CONNECT payload, Will properties, UTF-8 and binary)
unnumbered.review: Broker Cursor::text uses Rust strict UTF-8, rejects NUL, controls and noncharacters (the latter restrictions exceed the minimum); Cursor::binary preserves arbitrary payload/password/data bytes. Flags permit password without username in MQTT5. Client CLI restricts requested IDs to ASCII and validates Will topics, payload-format value and UTF-8 payload when indicator is 1; username rejects NUL/control characters. Broker Will property parsing enforces unique delay, expiry, format, content type, response topic and correlation data; User Properties remain ordered and repeatable. Delay defaults 0; Will expiry begins at publication via will_publication. TopicName rejects empty/wildcard response/Will topics; configured metadata bounds are additional implementation limits. PFI=1 Will validation by the server is optional; no mandatory server payload-UTF8 rejection is inferred. Will retain, QoS and metadata are stored together and transferred to routing; pending cancellation/publication is committed.
unnumbered.limitations: Client legacy password API uses strings, which limits inputs but still encodes valid Binary Data; arbitrary binary password support is not mandatory. General client persistence after closure remains a stated evidence gap. No power-loss or full Will/queue pressure campaign was executed.

unnumbered.review: serve_mqtt rejects malformed/unauthenticated/unauthorized CONNECT before registration or pipelined dispatch, checks ID length and required CONNACK budget, registers the session, writes CONNACK, then replays. Auth and Will ACL checks precede success. Takeover closes the previous connection via an actor close signal. Its missing 0x8E diagnostic remains P232-CONNECT-01 as a low-severity recommendation: the explicit MUST requires closure, while the diagnostic description refers to section 4.13, whose other-error handling permits closure without a DISCONNECT. The malformed/protocol-error diagnostic SHOULD in 4.13.1 is not assumed applicable to takeover. Router/session principal scoping is an intentional authorization boundary.
unnumbered.limitations: This agent ran no takeover probe. Parent-executed ../.artifacts/p232-broker-closes-1.json confirms previous-connection closure, absent diagnostic and a working new-connection ping in loopback open-lab; this finite observation is separate from the static judgment and does not prove all takeover races or full deployment security.

unnumbered.section: 3.2 (CONNACK format, properties, errors and session synchronization)
unnumbered.review: Broker CONNACK encoders use fixed valid reason/flags, unique bounded properties and no payload; success builders advertise size/alias/receive maximum as budgets permit, Shared Subscription Available=1 and default support for QoS2/retained/wildcards/subscription identifiers. Assigned IDs use collision-safe actor admission and mandatory-property budgeting. Client applies server keep alive, expiry and maximum packet size; it enforces alias bounds and checks assigned ID and selected subscription capabilities. Explicit client MUST deviations remain: max_qos and retain_available are parsed but never applied before publication; ordinary resume accepts Session Present=1 with fresh empty MqttState. Separate receiving-validation gaps: ConnAck::read ignores reserved acknowledge flag bits and does not reject leftover payload; ConnAckProperties::read overwrites most singleton properties, does not range-check booleans/max_qos/zero receive/max-packet-size, and does not require exact property-block consumption. read_mqtt_string enforces Unicode decoding but not MQTT NUL restrictions. Parent-supplied probes observe acceptance of malformed server input, including CONNACK User Property containing NUL. These observations support P232-CONNECT-04 as a receiving-validation gap/recommendation: section 4.13.1 gives the receiving Client a SHOULD response, not the Server's MUST close. They do not prove the client emits malformed CONNACK or independently violates an explicit MUST-close obligation. This agent inspected the parser and did not run those probes.
unnumbered.limitations: Root probe report ../.artifacts/p232-client-wire-2.json is current-task evidence reported by the parent, not historical CI or this agent's execution. Tested published client ELF came from source 1d60d38, SHA256 b9f2fa67c4c4d7263966097cd048627929b59d161b436d1b23e6005edac872f0; parent reports CLI/src, vendor and dependencies unchanged through baseline e03c5a46 (bridge-only differences). Broader malformed property cases are static findings, not independently executed probes here. Report 1 has a harness bug and is not used.

unnumbered.review: The normative body contains malformed identifier text valuesT-3.2.2-8], adjacent to the rule requiring a listed CONNACK reason code. The catalog's canonical MQTT-3.2.2-8 occurs in Appendix B. Retained exactly one canonical ledger row, classified against the main-body rule; no alias row or extra MUST was invented.
unnumbered.limitations: The literal malformed token is a source anomaly, not a new requirement. Exact force for 3.1.2-12 is permission ('can' for the three valid Will QoS values); its MAY ledger classification is not an invented mandatory statement.

unnumbered.review: Broker rejects AUTH reserved flags before body processing, validates unique Method/Data/Reason String, repeatable UTF-8 User Properties and full frame consumption. Its negotiated PLAIN flow accepts client Re-authenticate=0x19 and emits Success=0x00; no other enhanced method or initial challenge loop is claimed. Client patched FixedHeader::packet_type validates AUTH flags; AuthProperties::read rejects duplicate singletons and property-length mismatch; typed reason enum limits emitted codes. Both senders omit diagnostics and bound full AUTH size by the peer maximum. Client PLAIN reauthenticate requires success with matching method. General ordinary client loops can ignore unsolicited AUTH after a non-authenticated CONNECT: receiving-side semantic rejection is not uniformly established. The broker properly closes if AUTH is received without negotiated PLAIN.
unnumbered.limitations: Enhanced authentication is optional; absence of SCRAM/Kerberos challenge loops is not itself a deviation for one-shot PLAIN. Zero-length AUTH is decoded as Success by the patched library, but PLAIN CLI still demands its negotiated Method. No generic capability for arbitrary Auth API callers is claimed.

unnumbered.review: Inspected main-body method agreement, initial client data, continuation codes, rejection/closure, method echo and reauthentication rules. Only TLS PLAIN with initial data is supported; broker rejects other methods/legacy credential ambiguity before state, verifies credentials against the transport/policy principal, and refuses identity changes or security-generation mismatch during reauthentication. Successful CONNACK/AUTH echo PLAIN. CLI sends initial PLAIN data, waits for CONNACK, validates echo, and optionally performs one reauthentication before normal I/O; failures drop the connection. Challenge-code clauses are explicitly inapplicable to this one-shot mechanism, not treated as unreviewed success. Non-PLAIN/TLS restrictions are implementation choices within optional enhanced authentication.
unnumbered.limitations: This is a static audit of protocol/method state transitions, not a credential-strength, TLS deployment or side-channel certification. No credentials, operator state or private keys were read. No new dynamic security test or public PoC was created.

findings.summary: Broker takeover omits the described Session taken over diagnostic; mandatory closure is supported and no MUST-send violation is established.
findings.next_action: If clearer peer diagnostics are desired, consider a separately scoped change to convey bounded takeover reason 0x8E through the actor. Do not treat its current absence as a proven mandatory protocol violation: 3.1.4-3 explicitly requires closing, and 4.13.2 permits closing without DISCONNECT. Parent-executed ../.artifacts/p232-broker-closes-1.json observes closure and successful new-connection ping without a diagnostic; this agent only inspected that report.

findings.summary: Client sends publications that exceed server Maximum QoS or request forbidden retained storage because parsed CONNACK capabilities are ignored.
findings.next_action: Track an independently scoped client fix to retain/apply validated CONNACK capabilities before all regular and durable publish paths. Static inspection agrees with parent-reported failures in ../.artifacts/p232-client-wire-2.json; this agent did not execute the probes.

findings.summary: Ordinary client resume can proceed with Session Present although the fresh invocation has no local MQTT session state.
findings.next_action: Separate runtime prompt should validate local session ownership before continuing; keep Linux durable-mode handling and its intentional error/close behavior. Static finding; no dynamic assertion for this specific condition.

findings.summary: Client CONNACK receiving validation accepts malformed server input; this establishes a validation gap, not an explicit client MUST violation.
findings.next_action: Recommend focused validation coverage for singleton uniqueness, exact property boundaries, reserved flags/payload, value domains and MQTT UTF-8 constraints. Parent reports NUL User Property acceptance and nonminimal CONNACK VBI acceptance in ../.artifacts/p232-client-wire-2.json; the other cases are statically established parser gaps and were not dynamically executed by this agent. The fake server supplies the malformed packet: this does not demonstrate invalid CONNACK emission by the client or an independent client MUST-close violation. Receiving-client error handling is SHOULD under section 4.13.1; assess any justified exception and hardening separately from mandatory capability/session deviations.

findings.summary: Full client session-state preservation and uniform receiving-side diagnostic/authentication validation remain incompletely established.
findings.next_action: Document supported lifetime/termination modes and perform a separately scoped state-retention review plus targeted receiving-side error probes. Positive expiry and durable journals do not by themselves demonstrate every client state path.
